data.name: Episicava - Vol. 1
data.detailed_description:
Story
Fifty years ago, the face of the Earth was permanently changed when it came into contact with a mysterious force known as the “Alpha Nebula.” As a result, humans developed various supernatural abilities and divided themselves based on those traits.
The main factions include: The Tonitrui, the Excedente, the Praecantator, the Permuto, and the Northmanni. Each has their own unique set of abilities that came with the collision – with the exception of the Northmanni, who remain largely unchanged.
Among these races, however, existed a special group of people who managed to retain all the other races’ abilities. They were a very powerful - but small and isolated group - known as “Emulators.”
Arin Arlento was one of these people, living in a remote village with his grandfather and other members of their race; everything was peaceful until the Northmanni Empire massacred the Emulators and kidnapped his childhood friend, Aria.
The only other survivor, Arin escaped into the Northmanni’s home continent of Rakos, hiding and plotting his revenge – that is, until he found out that Aria was still alive and was being experimented on.
Loathing the world that took everything away from him, Arin begins his quest to retrieve his friend and exact retribution on those who destroyed all that he held dear.
It’s one misguided man against the world…

About
Betrayed, defeated, and left alone in the cruel wilderness, the story follows our protagonist, Arin Arlento, and his quest for retribution; one that questions friendship, revenge, and human nature itself. Surrounded by a cast of quirky heroines, the story features a selection of scenes which range from slice of life to heart-breaking sadness to nail-biting action.

Features
Volume one features roughly 5-10 hours of play arising from a word count of more 150K+, more than 40 CGs and 20+ music tracks. The first volume contains the common route progressions through the tribes of Fulgur and Tribus, as well as Aniam and Alacria's routes.

data.short_description: Inspired by classic visual novels such as Fate/Stay Night, Episicava is an action/adventure story following Arin Arlento and his female companions as they navigate their world’s treacherous dangers and wonderful sights, constantly under the pressure of a greater evil.

reviews.review:
[i]* A free key of the game was given to me. Even so, that didn’t affect my opinion of the final product.[/i]

[i]Episicava Vol.1[/i] is a medium-length action visual novel by [url=https://twitter.com/WorksEpic]Epic Works[/url]. Episicava tells the story of a young man called Arin Arlento and his search of revenge against the people that murdered his entire village and family. Also in this world, humans have superpowers and are divided depending on their abilities. [b]Please notice that this is the first game of a trilogy.[/b]

The story starts right out with action. But I disliked the fact that there was a lot of information being thrown at the reader right in the beginning as well, like a full explanation of how the superpowers work; that could've been explained during the novel. The story progresses at a fast pace too, with a lot of new characters showing up. This title is also mostly kinetic, there will be a few choices to make from time to time in order to avoid bad endings. There are two heroine routes in this first volume: Alacria and Aniam. Alacria is your typical tsundere girl and Aniam is more mature, I personally liked her better and her route as well. An important detail is that you'll have to read Alacria's route first to unlock Aniam's, so if you're not a big fan of tsundere type, you'll have to bear with Alacria for a while. After clearing Aniam's good ending, you'll unlock the "true route" of the game.

There is one critical factor that plagues Episicava to the core: the clichés. They are [i]everywhere[/i]. I'm used to them, I usually don't mind as long as the story is good and the characters are likable. But there are so many clichés in this visual novel that it became a bit overwhelming at some point in my opinion, and that can be a huge let down for some people. We already have the "revenge setting" of the story, all the girls love Arin, one time or another he'll release his "true power", there are hundreds of complicated names that you won't remember anymore after 2 minutes, and so on. The writing feels like it was based on a s*hiton of shonen manga, all at once.

Let's talk about the technical aspects. The art was good/average. But it was very inconsistent, and that was a let down to me. The CG quality is different from each other and from the sprites, it's simply a different art style. If all the images had the same quality of the CGs or sprites, I wouldn't complain. I just don't like inconsistency regarding art in a visual novel, that's a huge pet peeve of mine. Also, Alacria's sprite is missing the rest of her legs; she's literally floating when she appears on the screen. o_o
I must say that I [b]loved[/b] the backgrounds, though. Honestly, they were so pretty and colorful, maybe one of the best backgrounds I've seen in a western visual novel so far. I also liked the little animations that were presented during the action scenes as well, they were nice. The BGM was good too. The songs are catchy and exciting but along the way sometimes they sound misplaced. Maybe it's just me, I don't know. I rarely talk about the UI, but I think this is worth mentioning: There's this giant circle with lots of symbols right beside the text box that one time or another will glow depending on how Arin uses his powers. The standard blue text box is alright, but that giant symbol just annoys me. I thought it would have some sort of major impact in the gameplay, but it apparently doesn't have. By the way, there's a bug in the gallery: when I try to see the CGs I've collected in the "others" category, it doesn't matter how many times I click on the thumbnail, the full image won't show up... Anyway, this game is fairly long, it took me almost nine hours to read the common route, both heroine routes, and the true route. 

6/10. I recommend getting this game on a sale since the writing style might not please everyone. I know that I've pointed out a lot of flaws, but that doesn't mean that I hated this title. It had its moments, it certainly isn't the worst visual novel I've played, but it's far from the best. I think there's a lot of room to improve here since the essence of the story is interesting. I wish good luck to the developers on their next releases! [spoiler](There's also a [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/618430/discussions/0/1694917906649519801/]"special patch"[/url] that unlocks extra content ( ͡o ͜ʖ ͡o))[/spoiler]
